{{Short description|German mathematician}}
{{Notability|1=Biographies|date=September 2024}}

'''Hans Hefer''' (born on 27 February 1907<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hartmann |first1=Uta |title=Heinrich Behnke (1898-1979): zwischen Mathematik und deren Didaktik |language=de|date=2009 |publisher=Lang |isbn=9783631588604 |page=338 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ow7JRKb6ND8C |access-date=11 November 2024}}</ref> and died on 22 November 1941, [[Eastern Front (World War II)|Eastern Front]]<ref name="MUFB"/>) was a German mathematician who worked on [[several complex variables]]. [[Hefer's lemma]] or [[Hefer's theorem]] bear his name.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boas |first1=Harold |title=Math 685 Notes Topics in Several Complex Variables |url=https://haroldpboas.gitlab.io/courses/685-2005c/notes.pdf |access-date=19 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |url={{Google books|bL8jDwAAQBAJ|pg=136|plainurl=yes}}| title=Function Theory of Several Complex Variables | isbn=9780821827246 | last1=Krantz | first1=Steven George | year=2001 | publisher=American Mathematical Soc. }}</ref>

==Life==
There is not sufficient documentation regarding the life of Hans Hefer. 
Hefer is known to have earned a Ph.D. at the [[University of Münster]] in 1941, supervised by [[Heinrich Behnke]].<ref name="MUFB">{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/FB10/historie/anhanga.pdf|title=
A Mathematische Dissertationen bis 1945| publisher= Universität Münster Fachbereich Mathematik und Informatik|access-date=22 October 2024|quote=}}--''A list of mathematics doctoral degrees until 1945 awarded by University of Münster's mathematics and informatics department.''</ref><ref>{{mathgenealogy|139142}}</ref> 

In a posthumous publication made by [[Karl Stein (mathematician)|Karl Stein]] and [[Heinrich Behnke|Heinrich Benke]] with Hefer's name in ''Mathematische Annalen'' in 1950/51, it was written in a footnote that the author had fallen in the [[Eastern Front (World War II)|East]] and the article is an excerpt from his dissertation which he defended in 1940.<ref>{{Cite journal| url=http://eudml.org/doc/160216| author= Hans Hefer| title=Zur Funktionentheorie mehrerer Veränderlichen. Über eine Zerlegung analytischer Funktionen und die Weilsche Integraldarstellung|journal= Mathematische Annalen|pages=276–278|volume = 122|year = 1950–51| issue= 3| doi= 10.1007/BF01342970|access-date= 22 October 2024}}</ref> It was also added there that ''Since 1941, papers by [[Kiyoshi Oka|K. Oka]] and [[Henri Cartan|H. Cartan]] have appeared that contain Hefer's results but use different proofs.''
